idiom_name: @Mapper interface with toMessage/fromMessage, invoked by the endpoint
implementation_notes: MapStruct generates the mapper at build time: an @Mapper interface declaring OrderMessage toMessage(Order) and Order fromMessage(OrderMessage), with @Mapping for fields whose names or types differ, becomes a plain-Java implementation that a renamed property turns into a build failure instead of a silently dropped field. The endpoint (@JmsListener, MessageListener, Kafka consumer) injects the mapper and invokes it; the message DTO is a separate type that Jackson, a Jakarta Messaging BytesMessage or a Kafka serialiser encodes, and the entity is never handed to the serialiser.
pitfalls: A generated mapper cannot decide policy: absent-versus-default, unit conversion and unknown enum values need @Mapping(defaultExpression=...) or a qualified method, otherwise the generated code takes the silent null path.
Mapping a lazy JPA association triggers queries or LazyInitializationException outside the transaction: map from a loaded aggregate or an id, never through a proxy.
Jackson serialises getters you did not intend; keep the message DTO free of domain types and navigation properties so its shape is what gets published.

variants.name: Message record plus hand-written mapper class
variants.idiom_name: record message contract with compact-constructor invariants and a final mapper class
variants.implementation_notes: On a modern LTS the message is a record and the mapper is a small final class with static toMessage(Order) / fromMessage(OrderMessage) methods, so the mapping has one owner and the record's compact constructor rejects malformed payloads (blank id, negative total) at construction. Choose it when annotation processors are not welcome in the messaging module or when the conversion has real logic that generated code cannot express; records also give value equality, which makes golden-message tests read naturally.
pitfalls: Records are shallowly immutable: a record holding a mutable collection still exposes shared mutable state to the consumer.
Serialisation libraries need explicit record support (Jackson 2.12+ or a custom serialiser); pin the version rather than falling back to a mutable POJO with setters.
The compact constructor runs on both inbound and outbound construction: keep it to boundary invariants, not business rules that only apply to consumed messages.
